 Where does UND sit in the FCS playoff picture?
 The Fighting Hawks will try for an eighth win against Southern Illinois on Saturday
 UND wide receiver Deng Deng celebrates a first-half touchdown against Tennessee Tech on Saturday, Nov. 29, 2025, in Cookeville, Tenn. Leighton Chamblee / UND Athletics 
 By 
 Tom Miller

 GRAND FORKS — Already with seven Division I wins and two Top 10 victories, the UND football program has been considered a lock to make the FCS playoff field, which will be announced Sunday at 11 a.m. on ESPNU.
 The No. 10-ranked and 7-4 Fighting Hawks will face Southern Illinois at 1 p.m. Saturday at the Alerus Center in the regular-season finale.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Although the Hawks appear to be a lock for the 24-team field, there's varying opinion on where UND could be seeded. 
 The FCS playoff committee, which includes UND athletic director Bill Chaves, will seed the top 16 seeds in the tournament with the top eight seeds receiving a first-round bye for Thanksgiving weekend.
 Whereas a few years ago, the FCS' first-round matchups were based on a bidding process, the committee now dictates which teams earn those opportunities via seeds. Nearly all projections of UND from FCS analysts have UND hosting a playoff game, likely assuming a win over SIU.
 The playoff committee has released two rankings during the season. UND was slated at No. 6 in the first rankings released in October, then fell out of the Top 8 in the second release in early November after back-to-back road losses at Top 10 foes South Dakota and Youngstown State.
 But since those rankings, UND responded with a 28-point win over then-No. 10 Illinois State, which responded the following week with a road win at highly regarded Youngstown State.
 The Stats Perform FCS Top 25 poll is not used by the playoff committee to determine seeding.
 With one week of results to go, many of the national projections have slated UND just outside the Top 8. However, UND's strong stretch of schedule and the Hawks' claim of the only FCS team to beat South Dakota State could be compelling arguments to sneak in to the Top 8.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 For UND, two key matchups this week around the FCS will include No. 8 Montana at No. 2 Montana State in the Brawl of the Wild and No. 7 South Dakota at No. 11 Illinois State.
 Montana State defending turf in Bozeman would help UND push the Griz away from a Top 8 seed. Meanwhile, Illinois State beating South Dakota could help UND on a couple of fronts: make UND's recent dominant win over the Redbirds look better to the committee and make it difficult for committee members to seed Illinois State — possibly at No. 8 — directly above UND when the two teams recently met head-to-head with a lopsided outcome.
 From there, it remains to be seen if committee members will consider some of the context of UND's season. The Hawks lost in overtime in Vermillion and led nearly the whole way at Youngstown before losing on fourth-and-19 late in the fourth quarter. 
 The playoff committee has also made past precedence of considering key injuries when evaluating a season. UND's worst loss, at Northern Iowa, ended with UND standout quarterback Jerry Kaminski spending the fourth quarter on crutches.
